source: SemanticALLI: Caching Reasoning, Not Just Responses, in Agentic Systems
summary: Caches structured intermediate representations (IRs) of agent reasoning stages rather than monolithic prompt/response pairs, achieving 83.10% hit rate vs 38.7% for monolithic caching, with 2.66 ms median retrieval latency. Key insight: decompose planning into canonicalization + synthesis steps and cache each independently.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses the costly fresh-LLM-call-per-run pattern in Planning stage; AgentForge's existing similarity.ts and artifactRepository make this immediately implementable

source: Viston Tech — Monitoring Strategy for AI Agent Systems in 2026
summary: 2026 enterprise guide advocating proactive governance-by-architecture for agent workflows, with stale-state escalation as a documented baseline: stuck steps should trigger real notifications with context attached, not silent failures.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge has no automated escalation for runs stuck in AwaitingPlanApproval, HumanClarificationNeeded, or AIBlocked; this pattern directly addresses that gap

source: UptimeRobot — AI Agent Monitoring: Best Practices, Tools & Metrics for 2026
summary: Comprehensive 2026 monitoring guide establishing per-state TTL escalation and stuck-step notification as production standards for agentic systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — secondary source supporting HID-183 stale-run health monitor design

source: AIware 2026 — Examining LLMs Ability to Summarize Code Through Mutation-Analysis
summary: Validates LLMs' ability to interpret mutation testing reports and generate targeted test improvements, establishing mutation analysis as a practical quality gate for AI-generated code.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — supports HID-185 mutation-score gate at AIReview; AgentForge's AI-generated tests may share model blind spots with AI-generated code, making mutation gating especially important

source: Augment Code — Mutation Testing for AI-Generated Code: A Practical Guide
summary: Practical 2026 guide establishing mutation testing as the standard for detecting tautological tests in AI-generated code; cites Meta's deployment across Facebook/Instagram/WhatsApp with 73% engineer acceptance rate.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — secondary source supporting HID-185; confirms production viability of StrykerJS-based mutation gating in TypeScript CI pipelines

source: Why Agent Caching Fails: Structured Intent Canonicalization with Few-Shot Learning
summary: Identifies the 'embedding similarity trap' in semantic caching (semantically close queries can require different tool sequences) and proposes structured intent canonicalization to improve cache precision.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — informs the fingerprinting design for HID-184; warns against naive cosine similarity on raw issue descriptions

source: TVCACHE: A Stateful Tool-Value Cache for Post-Training LLM Agents
summary: Caches tool-call results keyed by structured tool invocations in LLM agents, avoiding redundant external API calls within and across sessions.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge agents don't make external tool calls during execution (they work inside the CLI subprocess), but the per-tool caching pattern could apply to git/test operations

source: Letta / MemGPT Three-Tier Memory Architecture 2026
summary: Mature three-tier OS-inspired agent memory model (core/archival/recall) with active memory management via tool calls. Anthropic 'Dreaming' (May 2026) and Google Memory Bank (I/O 2026) follow this architecture.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses limitation #7 (no agent memory across runs); however, this topic is already deeply covered by HID-17, HID-23, HID-36, HID-40, HID-44, HID-112, HID-131, HID-145, HID-161, HID-180 and many more

source: Hippocampus: Efficient and Scalable Memory Module for LLM Agents
summary: Plug-in memory module scaling to millions of stored episodes using hierarchical indexing. Proposes hippocampal-consolidation patterns for cross-session agent memory.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — architectural detail for cross-run memory; already covered thematically by existing backlog issues

source: Mem-α: Learning Memory Construction via Reinforcement Learning
summary: Trains a policy via RL to decide which observations from an agent run are worth writing to memory (store/summarize/discard), rather than using heuristic rules.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — addresses memory construction quality; covered thematically by distillation pipeline issues (HID-119, HID-127, HID-180)

source: Choosing How to Remember: Adaptive Memory Structures for LLM Agents
summary: Frames memory construction as a decision (replace/append/summarize/discard) learned from downstream task performance. Companion to Mem-α.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — memory write policy; covered thematically by existing distillation issues

source: MetaSkill-Evolve: Recursive Two-Timescale Skill Improvement
summary: Two-timescale self-improvement loop: fast timescale refines individual skills from task outcomes; slow timescale evolves the meta-skill that selects/composes skills. Uses Allocator/Proposer/Evolver architecture evaluated on OfficeQA, SealQA, ALFWorld.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — maps to versioned prompt templates with A/B testing; however already covered by HID-70 (credit-assigned prompt template evolution with A/B tracking) and HID-137 (run-outcome-driven stage prompt evolution)

source: Skill-MAS: Evolving Meta-Skill for Automatic Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Extends MetaSkill-Evolve to multi-agent systems; skills govern which agent handles which subtask and how agents communicate.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — single-agent stages in AgentForge reduce applicability; agent routing aspect covered by model-routing issues

source: Retrospective Progress-Aware Self-Refinement
summary: After each run, agent scores its own partial progress and produces a structured critique that feeds into the next attempt, avoiding full restart.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses limitation #3 (no plan repair); however covered by HID-130 (automated failure post-mortem reflection and smart retry), HID-138 (structured trajectory snapshot on failure)

source: Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster Agentic Systems
summary: Draft agent tentatively executes predicted next actions while a verifier catches up asynchronously; lossless 1.8x–3.7x wall-clock speedups. Reports 35–61% of total agent time spent on tool execution.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses limitation #9 (no speculative execution); covered by HID-101 (speculative implementation skeleton during plan-review idle), HID-47 (speculative next-stage pre-staging)

source: Cost-Aware Speculative Execution for LLM-Agent Workflows (PASTE)
summary: PASTE mines historical execution traces for recurring tool-call patterns and pre-executes speculatively when pattern fires; adds five-dimension cost model (latency, tokens, failure prob, opportunity cost, cancellation cost) for profitable speculation decisions. Up to 6x cost reduction reported.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — pattern-stable AgentForge stages are ideal PASTE targets; covered by HID-148 (pattern-aware subprocess pre-spawn to hide stage startup latency)

source: Anytime Verified Agents (AVA)
summary: Dynamically allocates compute across search breadth, sampling count, and verification depth within a user-specified budget; selective verification cascades with early exits. Key result: smart allocation beats 4x brute-force compute.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses limitation #6 (no test-time compute scaling); covered by HID-169 (budget-aware dynamic stage timeouts from task complexity signals), HID-129 (token-budget-aware adaptive granularity)

source: ZEBRA: Zero-Shot Budgeted Resource Allocation for LLM Orchestration
summary: Zero-shot prompting strategy that asks the model to predict its own compute needs before task start, then binds the orchestrator to that budget. Enables cost-aware scheduling and model-tier selection.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — addresses limitations #1 and #6; already created as HID-158 (per-phase token budget allocation inspired by ZEBRA water-filling algorithm)

source: BAGEN: Are LLM Agents Budget-Aware?
summary: Benchmark testing whether agents can estimate mid-execution how much budget remains and whether the task is still finishable within it; establishes pass/fail metrics for budget-aware agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — evaluation framework for budget-aware implementation; thematically covered by HID-146 (budget-aware early-stop gate) and HID-124

source: pass@k vs pass^k metrics and trace-based evaluation (Confident AI, Braintrust 2026)
summary: 2026 standard: pass^k (success in every k runs) as the production reliability metric; trace-based evaluation scoring full execution trajectories not just final outputs. Langfuse, Arize, AgentOps, Braintrust provide TS SDKs.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — addresses limitation #4 (no agent performance tracking); covered by HID-142 (OpenTelemetry GenAI spans), HID-166 (per-stage telemetry and analytics), HID-133, HID-52

source: In-Context Prompting Obsoletes Agent Orchestration for Procedural Tasks
summary: April 2026 paper arguing that single well-structured in-context prompts consistently outperform multi-stage orchestration for procedural/well-defined tasks on both success rate and cost; proposes a task classifier routing simple issues to a single-stage fast path.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium-High — fast-path routing for simple issues is genuinely novel vs. backlog; closest is HID-50 (confidence-based optional stage elision) which is within-run elision, not pre-run routing; also relates to HID-175 (complexity-signal model routing)

source: Karpathy — Agentic Engineering Framework (2026)
summary: Karpathy declares 'agentic engineering' as the successor to vibe coding; five core skills: spec design, diff review, eval design, security oversight, quality taste. Identifies eval design (verifiable feedback loops) as the central skill gap.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — validates AgentForge's architecture and identifies eval/feedback loop as the key gap; not a specific implementable enhancement but strong directional signal

source: ByteDance DeerFlow 2.0
summary: #1 GitHub Trending Feb 27 2026; lead-agent-to-parallel-subagents pattern with isolated contexts, configurable timeouts per sub-agent, skills registry, persistent memory, sandboxed filesystem. Python/LangGraph.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium-High — sub-agent isolation and per-subprocess termination conditions are relevant to plan repair; Python-based so not directly adoptable, but patterns are transferable; parallel execution covered by HID-136

source: Mastra — TypeScript-Native Agent Framework
summary: Breakout TS-native agent framework mid-2026 (88+ releases): graph-based workflow orchestration, streaming tool arguments, memory via @mastra/mem0, evals, tracing, playground. Native Fastify-compatible server.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — TypeScript stack match; incremental adoption possible via WorkflowStep wrappers; addresses streaming, retry, checkpoint gaps simultaneously; but adopting Mastra would be a significant refactor not a targeted enhancement

source: LangGraph Q2 2026: TimeoutPolicy, DeltaChannel, v2 Streaming, Error Handlers
summary: Q2 2026 LangGraph releases: per-node TimeoutPolicy (run_timeout/idle_timeout), node-level error handlers routing to recovery nodes (Saga pattern), DeltaChannel cutting checkpoint overhead 70%, v2 typed streaming API with per-token visibility.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — TimeoutPolicy maps to HID-147; error handlers map to HID-168; DeltaChannel not applicable (no LangGraph); streaming covered by HID-125; all patterns already captured as AgentForge-native issues

source: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 GA (AutoGen + Semantic Kernel merger)
summary: GA April 2026; unified async event-driven framework with A2A task execution protocol for structured agent handoffs and HITL flow checkpoints. Replaces AutoGen maintenance mode.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — A2A protocol relevant if AgentForge adds mid-issue agent handoffs; HITL checkpoints partially covered by existing approval states; Python primary so not directly adoptable

source: Self-Healing Agentic Orchestrators (arXiv:2606.01416)
summary: Separates agent execution into data plane (agent work) and reliability control plane (monitors, classifies failures, selects recovery actions with budget, verifies recovered trajectories). Achieves 98.8% task success vs 94.5% retry-only.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — control plane/data plane separation maps to Fastify orchestrator vs CLI subprocess; recovery action menu is elegant; covered thematically by HID-168 (targeted failure-recovery loop), HID-181 (adaptive fault recovery)

source: GraSP: Graph-Structured Skill Compositions for Agent Repair
summary: Five local repair primitives: Rebind, InsertPrereq, Substitute, Rewire, Bypass. Fixes failures at the skill level before escalating to global replanning; circuit-breaker pattern based on historical failure rates per (issue-type, stage) combination.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — five primitives are a concrete taxonomy for failure recovery; covered by HID-144 (execution-trace plan repair without full reset) and HID-168 (targeted failure-recovery loop)

source: Temporal Workflow Streams for Real-Time Agent Output
summary: Temporal's Replay 2026 Workflow Streams provide durable real-time output channel without separate Redis/SSE infrastructure; combined with Claude Code stream-json and OpenAI run_streamed, full per-token streaming is now documented production pattern.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly addresses limitation #8 (no streaming); covered by HID-48 (stream agent subprocess output as SSE events) and HID-125 (stream incremental agent progress events to dashboard)

source: Agentic Reinforced Policy Optimization (arXiv:2507.19849)
summary: RLVR (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards) applied to agentic orchestration; uses binary verifiable rewards (test pass/fail, compilation success) to train orchestration policies.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — applies to using test outcomes as formal reward signals; covered by HID-172 (emit replayable orchestration-decision traces as RL training corpus)

source: ReleaseEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs in Automated Release Note Generation
summary: Benchmark and methodology for evaluating LLM-generated release notes from code diffs and commit histories. Covers translating developer language to user-facing language.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — release note generation from completed runs is a useful UX feature but not a core orchestration gap; none of the listed limitations directly addressed
